# trackly (tck)

> A local-first, Toggl-style time-tracking CLI for freelancers and
> contractors. No account, no browser, no subscription: a single SQLite
> database plus a command-line tool.

## What it does

- `tck start` / `tck stop`: run a timer, or `tck add` a completed entry
  with an explicit time range.
- Workspaces isolate projects, tags, and entries per client so hours never
  mix across clients.
- Hourly rates resolve project -> workspace and freeze on each entry, so a
  later rate change never repriced past work.
- `--client` filters reports, exports, invoices, and earnings across every
  project that client owns.
- `tck report pdf`, `tck export csv`, and `tck report chart` (ANSI, in the
  terminal) share the same date/filter flags.
- `tck invoice pdf` generates PDF invoices priced from billable time, with
  tax and an auto-incrementing number template.
- `tck mcp` starts a Model Context Protocol server, exposing the same
  functionality as MCP tools so an AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude
  Code) can manage time tracking directly.

## Install

    npm install -g @tonyakitori/trackly

Requires Node.js >= 20. Binary name after install: `tck`.
